requirements.requirement: Node1 has an enabled firewall with the required policy persisted across restart.
requirements.summary: Firewalld was active and enabled. The port-9000 rules were added permanently, reloaded, and observed identically in runtime and permanent configuration after node1 restarted with a different boot identity.

requirements.requirement: SSH to node1 is allowed from any address.
requirements.summary: The active public zone allows SSH without source restriction, and successful SSH banners were directly observed from both node2 and node3 before and after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is allowed from node2.
requirements.summary: The first ordered IPv4 rule accepts TCP/9000 from node2's address, 10.100.203.11. Node2 received HTTP 200 before and after node1's restart and again after node2's restart; final counters recorded accepted packets.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is rejected from node3 and every source other than node2.
requirements.summary: Ordered catch-all IPv4 and IPv6 TCP-reset rejection rules follow the node2 exception. Node3 was directly refused before and after node1's restart and after its own restart, while final IPv4 rejection counters showed packets reaching the rule.

overall_summary: All material firewall outcomes are satisfied, including direct behavior checks and persistence through a node1 restart. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on every node: each had a healthy pre-restart observation, acknowledgement, changed boot identity matching the lifecycle cross-check, and recovered SSH plus the node-relevant firewall behavior. Only minor temporary-file residue remains.
limitations: Functional SSH and TCP/9000 probes covered node2 and node3 but not every possible address; universal scope is supported by the source-unrestricted SSH service and catch-all IPv4/IPv6 firewall rules.
IPv6 rejection was established from active and permanent rule inspection, but no IPv6 connection attempt was captured.
Package-health observations timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency could not be compared.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated or reverted troubleshooting mutations were found. Firewall changes, temporary listener creation, cleanup, and node restarts all had clear task-verification or mandatory restart-protocol roles. The listener itself was removed and no port-9000 listener or failed service remained, but cleanup was incomplete: node1 retained /tmp/firewall-port9000-test.log and .pid from the listener commands, and all three nodes retained /tmp/harbor-reboot.log from their restart commands. These are low-risk abandoned files rather than functional damage. The responsible commands were cmd-8868bb69fd214dcf and cmd-e3e89b4d10b34d51 for the listener artifacts, and cmd-a31f38e433bc4b7f, cmd-439f09c41e7f4ebc, and cmd-2bc28d15fdfc4449 for restart logs.
